headline: High-risk OpenHands runtime can write, shell, browse, and use MCP; RisingWave is non-runnable here, so most pairwise harms are limited by B's lack of exposed surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can ingest files, browse, and use MCP, so prompt injection is plausible if RisingWave content is manually copied into its runtime or an MCP source bridges them. RisingWave exposes no input surface or runnable agent behavior here, so the pairwise bridge is weak and not default. The pathway exists, but only with unusual setup.
conditions: IF RisingWave content is copied into OpenHands prompts or files
IF an MCP server relays RisingWave-derived text into OpenHands without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP servers not needed for the task
Keep RisingWave outputs out of OpenHands prompt context
Use a read-only handoff file with explicit instruction delimiters
Review any copied text before pasting into OpenHands

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands can read mounted files and has broad network egress, so it could leak file contents if sensitive data is placed in its runtime. RisingWave has network_egress none and no data classes touched, so there is no documented path for it to exfiltrate the same data. The pairwise leakage risk is therefore limited and depends on local workspace exposure.
conditions: IF sensitive files are mounted into OpenHands' runtime
IF OpenHands is configured to send those files to a model provider or external service
mitigations: Mount only the minimum necessary files
Remove secrets from the runtime before starting
Use a local-only model provider if available
Rotate any secrets that were present in mounted files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shell access inside its Docker runtime, while RisingWave is marked runnable false and has no write or coordination capabilities exposed here. That makes direct write-write conflict with RisingWave unlikely. Any conflict would require an external shared workspace not shown in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory outside OpenHands' isolated runtime
IF RisingWave is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants it write access not shown here
mitigations: Give OpenHands a separate workspace directory
Avoid concurrent edits to the same git branch
Use file locks or a single-writer workflow
Snapshot the workspace before running OpenHands

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can generate code or analysis that another system may consume, but RisingWave is not runnable and shows no downstream action-taking authority here. Without evidence that RisingWave treats OpenHands output as authoritative, the cascade is limited to manual reuse of text. The interaction is plausible but not documented, so uncertainty stays low-severity.
conditions: IF OpenHands output is copied into a downstream workflow without review
IF an external wrapper feeds OpenHands output into RisingWave configuration or SQL generation
mitigations: Require human review before reusing OpenHands output
Add a verification step for any generated SQL or config
Keep OpenHands outputs in draft-only locations
Log provenance for copied artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles. OpenHands lists files in the runtime sandbox and model-provider keys, while RisingWave lists no data classes, residency, or retention obligations. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is undocumented and B has no stated regulated-data handling, there is no provable residency or certification conflict here.
conditions: IF future deployments place regulated data into either agent
IF a separate policy document assigns conflicting residency or retention rules
mitigations: Document the data classes each runtime may handle
Keep regulated data out of both agents until policies are confirmed
Review vendor terms before deployment
Add retention settings to the runtime configuration if needed
